title: 5 Ways to Get Rich on a Normal Salary

lines.text: Your paycheck lands, and three weeks later, you're broke again.
lines.screen: Envelope drops into Stick's hands; calendar flips; bills fly in and carry the cash off; a moth flies out of his wallet.

lines.text: Rent took some. Food took some. A dozen little subscriptions took the rest. And you're left wondering where it all went.
lines.screen: Bills labelled RENT, FOOD, SUBS each grab a stack of cash and run.

lines.text: Stop blaming your salary.
lines.screen: Red stamp: IT'S NOT YOUR SALARY.

lines.text: It's five moves nobody showed you, and almost none of them cost a cent.
lines.screen: Five numbered circles pop up behind Stick; a $0 price tag swings in.

lines.text: Here's the plan. Five moves, one at a time, and each one feeds the next.
lines.screen: A road with five signposts; Stick walks onto it.

lines.text: By the end, you'll have the whole machine.
lines.screen: Ghost outline of a five-gear machine at the end of the road.

lines.text: Quick note. I'm a stick figure, not your financial advisor. This is education, not advice.
lines.screen: Small badge: Education, not financial advice.

lines.text: Move one. Pay yourself first.
lines.screen: Title card: 1 — PAY YOURSELF FIRST.

lines.text: Here's how most people do it. Paycheck comes in. You pay rent, food, fun, and whatever is left at the end, you save.
lines.screen: Coins flow into jars in order: RENT, FOOD, FUN, then SAVINGS last.

lines.text: Here's the thing. There is never anything left.
lines.screen: Savings jar empty; tumbleweed rolls past.

lines.text: So flip the order. The day your pay arrives, a fixed slice goes straight to savings, before you touch a cent.
lines.screen: Jars swap places; SAVINGS jumps to the front and fills first.

lines.text: Then you live on the rest.
lines.screen: Remaining coins split across the other jars.

lines.text: This works because of a weird trick of the brain. Money you never see, you don't miss. Put your savings in a separate account, one that doesn't show up every time you open your spending app.
lines.screen: Stick puts the savings jar in a safe behind a curtain; thought bubble: out of sight, out of mind.

lines.text: It doesn't have to be big. Start with a slice that doesn't hurt, and nudge it up every time you get a raise.
lines.screen: Slider labelled 'your slice' ticks up step by step.

lines.text: And automate it. Set up an automatic transfer, so willpower never gets a vote.
lines.screen: Phone with toggle AUTO-TRANSFER: ON; coins move on their own.

lines.text: Boring. And that's the point.
lines.screen: Stick shrugs, sips tea.

lines.text: Move two. Kill high-interest debt.
lines.screen: Title card: 2 — KILL HIGH-INTEREST DEBT.

lines.text: Saving money while you carry credit card debt is like filling a bucket with a hole in the bottom.
lines.screen: Stick pours water into a bucket; it drains out of a hole.

lines.text: Card interest compounds against you. For example, three thousand dollars at twenty-two percent a year costs you over seven hundred dollars in interest in a single year, if you don't pay it down.
lines.screen: Label: EXAMPLE — $3,000 at 22% APR → over $700 interest in one year.

lines.text: That's money you worked for, buying absolutely nothing.
lines.screen: Bills fly into a monster labelled INTEREST.

lines.text: So, list your debts. Pay the minimum on all of them, and throw every spare dollar at the one with the highest interest rate.
lines.screen: Three cards with rates; the highest one is highlighted and smashed with a hammer.

lines.text: When it's gone, roll that payment into the next one. It speeds up, like a snowball.
lines.screen: The freed payment rolls into the next card, growing like a snowball.

lines.text: Some people prefer to clear the smallest balance first, for the quick win. That's fine too. The best plan is the one you'll actually stick with.
lines.screen: Two paths labelled HIGHEST RATE and SMALLEST BALANCE both reach a flag labelled DEBT FREE.

lines.text: And while you're digging out, stop adding new debt. You can't empty a bath with the tap still running.
lines.screen: Bathtub with the tap running; Stick turns it off.

lines.text: And keep a small emergency fund, so one flat tire doesn't put you right back on the card.
lines.screen: Car with a flat tyre; Stick pays from an EMERGENCY jar instead of a card.

lines.text: Move three. Invest early, and let time do the heavy lifting.
lines.screen: Title card: 3 — INVEST EARLY.

lines.text: Compounding means your money earns money, and then that money earns money too.
lines.screen: A snowball rolls downhill, growing.

lines.text: Watch. This is me. I put two hundred dollars a month into a low-cost index fund, starting at twenty-five.
lines.screen: Stick with tag: $200/month from age 25.

lines.text: This is Larry. Larry does the exact same thing, but he waits until he's thirty-five.
lines.screen: Larry, a blue stick figure, appears: $200/month from age 35.

lines.text: To keep the math simple, let's assume seven percent a year on average. That's an assumption, not a promise. Real markets jump around.
lines.screen: Label: ASSUMED 7% a year average (not guaranteed).

lines.text: At sixty-five, Larry has put in seventy-two thousand dollars, and ends up with about two hundred and forty thousand.
lines.screen: Larry's bar grows: put in $72k → about $244k.

lines.text: I put in ninety-six thousand. Only twenty-four thousand more. And I end up with about five hundred and twenty-five thousand.
lines.screen: Stick's bar towers: put in $96k → about $525k.

lines.text: Same habit. Ten extra years. More than double the money. The difference wasn't talent. It was time.
lines.screen: Big text: THE DIFFERENCE WAS TIME.

lines.text: And an index fund just means you own a tiny slice of hundreds of companies at once, so you're not betting everything on one.
lines.screen: A basket filled with tiny company buildings.

lines.text: And if your job offers a retirement plan with an employer match, take the full match first. It's the closest thing to free money you'll ever be offered.
lines.screen: Stick drops in a coin; the boss stick figure drops one in beside it: MATCH.

lines.text: Keep the fees low, keep adding, and don't panic sell when it drops. It will drop. Stay on the hill.
lines.screen: A jagged line chart trending up; Stick calmly holds on through the dips.

lines.text: Move four. Grow your income, then guard it.
lines.screen: Title card: 4 — GROW YOUR INCOME.

lines.text: Cutting costs has a floor. You can only skip so many coffees. But earning has no ceiling.
lines.screen: Left: arrow hits a floor labelled CUTTING. Right: arrow shoots up past the frame labelled EARNING.

lines.text: The best investment is usually you. A skill that's in demand. Getting really good at something people pay for.
lines.screen: Stick reads a book; a level-up bar fills.

lines.text: It doesn't take a degree. Ten minutes a day, every day, adds up to more than sixty hours of practice in a year.
lines.screen: A calendar fills with small ticks; counter: 10 min/day ≈ 60+ hours/year.

lines.text: Then use it. Ask for the raise, with proof. Switch jobs if yours won't pay what you're worth. Or start something on the side.
lines.screen: Three doors: RAISE, NEW JOB, SIDE PROJECT.

lines.text: But here's the trap. When income goes up, spending sneaks up right behind it.
lines.screen: Income bar rises; a bigger TV and a fancier car appear; savings stays at zero.

lines.text: So when you get a raise, send at least half of it straight to move one and move three. Live a little better, not a lot better.
lines.screen: Raise splits: half to SAVE and INVEST, half to LIFE.

lines.text: Move five. Own things that earn while you sleep.
lines.screen: Title card: 5 — OWN THINGS THAT EARN.

lines.text: There are two kinds of stuff. Things that take money out of your pocket, and things that put money into it.
lines.screen: Two columns: TAKES MONEY (car leaking cash) and MAKES MONEY (a tree growing coins).

lines.text: A new car loses value as soon as you drive it home. Shares in companies, a small business, things you create that keep selling. Those can pay you again and again.
lines.screen: Icons drop into the MAKES MONEY column: shares, a shop, a book.

lines.text: Your job trades hours for money, and you only have so many hours.
lines.screen: A clock; hours tick into coins one for one, then run out.

lines.text: Owning things breaks that link. That's how wealth stops depending on how hard you work today.
lines.screen: Stick naps in a hammock while the money tree drops coins.

lines.text: Start small. Ownership can be one share, or one thing you built on a weekend.
lines.screen: One share certificate and a tiny lemonade stand.

lines.text: And remember, the skills you built in move four are an asset too. Nobody can repossess what you know.
lines.screen: Stick taps his head; a gold star badge floats out.

lines.text: So that's the machine.
lines.screen: Five gears assemble into one machine.

lines.text: Pay yourself first, so money exists.
lines.screen: Gear 1 lights up.

lines.text: Kill the debt, so nothing leaks.
lines.screen: Gear 2 lights up.

lines.text: Invest it, so it grows.
lines.screen: Gear 3 lights up.

lines.text: Grow your income, so there's more to feed in.
lines.screen: Gear 4 lights up.

lines.text: And own things that earn, so it keeps going without you.
lines.screen: Gear 5 lights up; the machine spins and drops coins.

lines.text: Notice what's missing. No lottery. No hot tip. No coin your cousin swears is going to the moon.
lines.screen: Lottery ticket, hot-tip phone and rocket coin get crossed out.

lines.text: If anything promises you fast and guaranteed, run.
lines.screen: A shady stick figure in sunglasses holds a sign FAST + GUARANTEED; Stick runs.

lines.text: Getting rich is mostly boring stuff, done for a long time. And the earlier you start, the less boring stuff you need.
lines.screen: Stick back at the machine, calm.

scenes.chapter: What a real month looks like

lines.text: So what does this look like in a real month? Let's walk through one payday.
lines.screen: Calendar page: PAYDAY. Stick holds a paycheck.

lines.text: Day one. Pay lands. The automatic transfer moves your slice to savings, before you even wake up.
lines.screen: Coins slide to SAVINGS while Stick sleeps.

lines.text: Minimum payments go out on every debt, and the extra goes to the most expensive one.
lines.screen: Small coins to each card, a big coin to the highest-rate card.

lines.text: Another slice goes into your index fund. Same amount, every month, no matter what the news says.
lines.screen: Coin drops into the basket of companies; a TV yelling headlines is ignored.

lines.text: And what's left is yours. Rent, food, fun. No guilt, because the important stuff already happened.
lines.screen: Stick enjoys a pizza on the couch.

lines.text: Then you do it again next month. And the month after that. That's the whole trick.
lines.screen: Calendar pages flip faster and faster; the savings and investment bars grow.

lines.text: So here's your one job. Tonight, set up one automatic transfer. Any amount. That's move one, and the machine starts turning.
lines.screen: Phone: AUTO-TRANSFER ON. The machine's first gear starts turning.

lines.text: I'll see you in the next one.
lines.screen: Stick waves. End card.
